questions.stem: This myocardial histology field shows an inflammatory infiltrate among the cardiac muscle fibers. This lymphocytic pattern is most characteristic of which etiology of myocarditis?

explanation.summary: A predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate is characteristic of viral myocarditis; bacterial infection tends to produce neutrophilic infiltrates and hypersensitivity reactions produce eosinophilic infiltrates.
explanation.whyCorrect: A predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate is characteristic of viral myocarditis; bacterial infection tends to produce neutrophilic infiltrates and hypersensitivity reactions produce eosinophilic infiltrates.

questions.stem: This gross cross-section of a heart shows a spherical shape with markedly dilated ventricular cavities and thin walls. Which condition does it best demonstrate?

explanation.summary: The enlarged, spherical heart with dilated chambers and thin ventricular walls is the classic gross appearance of dilated cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enlarged, spherical heart with dilated chambers and thin ventricular walls is the classic gross appearance of dilated cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: This schematic depicts the sarcomere remodeling that produces chamber dilation in DCM. How are the new sarcomeres added to the cardiac muscle cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By net loss of existing sarcomeres

choices.label: B
choices.text: In parallel, side-by-side along the short axis

choices.label: C
choices.text: By fibrous replacement of the sarcomeres

choices.label: D
choices.text: In series, end-to-end along the long axis

choices.label: E
choices.text: By fatty infiltration between the sarcomeres

explanation.summary: Eccentric hypertrophy adds sarcomeres end-to-end (in series), lengthening the myocytes and dilating the chambers; parallel (side-by-side) addition instead produces the wall thickening of concentric hypertrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Eccentric hypertrophy adds sarcomeres end-to-end (in series), lengthening the myocytes and dilating the chambers; parallel (side-by-side) addition instead produces the wall thickening of concentric hypertrophy.
